We believe the future of enterprise AI will not be defined by static prompts or isolated APIs, but by companies that build compounding model advantages through proprietary data, fine-tuned behavior, and continuous improvement.

Who we are
Cohere Labs is Cohere's research lab that seeks to solve complex machine learning problems. We support fundamental research that explores the unknown, and are focused on creating more points of entry into machine learning research.

Our community is a space where researchers, engineers, linguists, social scientists and lifelong learners connect and collaborate with each other. We come together from all over the world and welcome you whether you are a mentor, dropout, just getting started, PhD, masters, undergraduate, unaffiliated, industry, academic or not really sure. We are excited to support community-driven research and to be shaped by our members' interests. 

Where we’ve come from
In 2017, a team of friends, classmates, and engineers started a distributed research collaboration, with a focus on creating a medium for early-career AI enthusiasts to engage with experienced researchers – they called it “for.ai.” Two of those co-founding members, Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang, later went on to co-found Cohere, and many of the founding members went on to do exciting things (pursuing PhDs, working at industry and academic labs). 

At the time, For AI was one of the first community-driven research groups to support independent researchers around the world. Today, Cohere is proud to reintroduce For AI as Cohere Labs, a dedicated research lab and community for exploring the unknown, together.

# Covenant AI

Covenant AI is a Technology, Information and Internet company. Covenant AI employs 6 people (+14.3% YoY, +1 person), founded in 2025. Its workforce is distributed across United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, and Canada.

## About

Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permis

properties.name: Covenant AI
properties.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

properties.name: Sodium
properties.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

properties.name: Forithmus
properties.description:
Forithmus is building medical intelligence.

Our mission is to develop generalist AI systems that can understand medical images and support clinicians across complex diagnostic workflows. By learning from large-scale medical imaging data and radiology reports, our models aim to help physicians interpret medical images faster, more consistently, and at global scale.

We believe one of the most important contributions of artificial intelligence in healthcare will be making physicians dramatically more productive and extending medical expertise to places where it is scarce.

Achieving this requires moving beyond narrow point solutions toward generalist medical AI systems that more closely mirror how clinicians interpret images in real clinical practice.

To accelerate progress toward medical intelligence, Forithmus develops large-scale datasets, foundation models, and research infrastructure for medical imaging, while collaborating openly with the global research and clinical community.

entity.name: Intelligence Cubed i³
entity.description:
Intelligence Cubed is building intelligence infrastructure that helps companies move from prompt-wrapper AI products to owned, fine-tuned model systems.

Most enterprise AI products today rely on generic foundation model APIs and prompt engineering, which makes it difficult for companies to own their model behavior, preserve domain expertise, reduce inference cost, or continuously improve from real user interactions. Intelligence Cubed solves this by turning product usage data into proprietary training assets and enabling companies to fine-tune, evaluate, deploy, and improve their own models over time.

Our platform helps teams collect, clean, label, approve, version, and evaluate high-quality training data from conversations, workflows, expert edits, user feedback, and business outcomes. Companies can then fine-tune owned models from approved behavior data, compare model versions, measure quality, latency, cost, and brand consistency, and deploy the best-performing models into production.

Beyond fine-tuning, Intelligence Cubed provides the evaluation, routing, deployment, and feedback-loop infrastructure needed to operate models continuously. We believe the future of enterprise AI will not be defined by static prompts or isolated APIs, but by companies that build compounding model advantages through proprietary data, fine-tuned behavior, and continuous improvement.

Our community is a space where researchers, engineers, linguists, social scientists and lifelong learners connect and collaborate with each other. We come together from all over the world and welcome you whether you are a mentor, dropout, just getting started, PhD, masters, undergraduate, unaffiliated, industry, academic or not really sure. We are excited to support community-driven research and to be shaped by our members' interests. 

Where we’ve come from
In 2017, a team of friends, classmates, and engineers started a distributed research collaboration, with a focus on creating a medium for early-career AI enthusiasts to engage with experienced researchers – they called it “for.ai.” Two of those co-founding members, Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang, later went on to co-found Cohere, and many of the founding members went on to do exciting things (pursuing PhDs, working at industry and academic labs). 

At the time, For AI was one of the first community-driven research groups to support independent researchers around the world. Today, Cohere is proud to reintroduce For AI as Cohere Labs, a dedicated research lab and community for exploring the unknown, together.

entity.name: Covenant AI
entity.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

entity.name: Sodium
entity.description:
Sodium builds the infrastructure for coordinating enterprise agents at scale.

Our flagship product is GEB-1, a world model that maintains a live representation of your organization’s goals, state, and operations. GEB-1 isn’t an LLM. It’s built on Active Inference, a framework from computational neuroscience in which a model continuously updates its beliefs from streaming observations and acts to minimize the gap between expectation and reality. Unlike pretrained models with frozen weights, GEB-1 learns online, in deployment.

GEB-1 is designed to work with Constellation, our distributed agent graph and runtime. Constellation operates hundreds or thousands of agents connected in a shared graph, coordinating with each other and with your human team. 

Security is structural: data flows only through explicit capability grants, so agents access exactly what they’re permitted to and nothing else.

GEB-1 connects to every agent in your Constellation, providing a single source of truth for memories, goals, and context across your organization. This addresses epistemic drift, the failure mode in naive agent frameworks where instructions, context, and reality fall progressively out of sync. GEB-1 grounds the system by inferring the state of your organization from live observations and updating each agent’s priors when its model of the world starts to drift.

Each customer gets a dedicated GEB-1 instance. Unlike shared frontier models, your GEB-1 learns exclusively from your organization, and both its data and learned parameters stay within your private deployment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

If you're an engineer, scientist, or researcher looking to work on hard problems, reach out: careers@na.ai

A jetty is a structure that extends into the sea — a launch point, a place of transition, a safe platform to move forward.

At a time when most companies are racing to automate everything, we’re asking:
What should AI do for humanity?
We believe the answer lies in building responsibly, testing rigorously, and creating jobs — not just replacing them.

We work with teams building copilots, agent workflows, retrieval systems, and memory-driven AI platforms that must operate reliably inside real environments with proprietary data.

We support companies designing and shipping:

• agentic workflow systems
• RAG and structured retrieval architectures
• temporal and persistent memory layers
• evaluation and safety pipelines
• private AI deployments and sovereign infrastructure
• enterprise copilots connected to internal systems

Alongside consulting engagements, we are building Thoth, a local-first runtime environment for agent workflows designed for organizations where sensitive data cannot leave their infrastructure.

Jetty AI operates as a small, deeply technical studio working across the US and India with a distributed engineering team focused on real-world AI deployment.

entity.description:
Forithmus is building medical intelligence.

Our mission is to develop generalist AI systems that can understand medical images and support clinicians across complex diagnostic workflows. By learning from large-scale medical imaging data and radiology reports, our models aim to help physicians interpret medical images faster, more consistently, and at global scale.

We believe one of the most important contributions of artificial intelligence in healthcare will be making physicians dramatically more productive and extending medical expertise to places where it is scarce.

Achieving this requires moving beyond narrow point solutions toward generalist medical AI systems that more closely mirror how clinicians interpret images in real clinical practice.

To accelerate progress toward medical intelligence, Forithmus develops large-scale datasets, foundation models, and research infrastructure for medical imaging, while collaborating openly with the global research and clinical community.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

      • a retail-only POS with payments

      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.

      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.

      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a

  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.
